kpis.label: Reference price
kpis.sub: Rs 131.69 = lowest listed-peer P/E in the DRHP (Escorts Kubota 23.35x, p. 156) x FY26 basic EPS Rs 5.64 (p. 154). It is our construct for measuring upside, not a price band. For scale: the Oct-2025 allotment to the promoters in the business transfer was Rs 1,547 per Rs 10 share, which is Rs 33.63 per Rs 5 share after the 22:1 bonus and 1:2 split (our arithmetic from pp. 105, 388).

focus.title: Cash flow vs profit
focus.detail: CFO was Rs 124.93 m / 130.15 m / 26.85 m in FY24 / FY25 / FY26. Cumulative CFO is Rs 281.93 m against cumulative PAT of Rs 404.39 m = 69.7% (mixed standalone / consolidated basis). FY26 CFO is 8.6% of FY26 PAT after a Rs 445.46 m inventory build and a Rs 281.35 m rise in other assets; the Rs 104.52 m of tax paid is also in CFO. CFO after interest paid (Rs 96.06 m) and lease payments (Rs 17.85 m) is negative in FY26 (-Rs 87.06 m).

focus.title: Related-party capex & subsidiaries
focus.detail: Related-party purchases Rs 164.91 m in FY26 (6.5% of cost of materials consumed) and sales Rs 69.99 m (1.7% of revenue); balance receivable from Guru Nanak Agriculture Implements Rs 49.09 m = 8.0% of trade receivables. Loans and advances given to KMP at 31-Mar-2026: Jagatjit Singh Rs 45.00 m and Dharam Singh Rs 10.00 m (p. 95). The Rs 716.64 m capex object is on the Dehlon facility, whose land (16.20 acres) is leased from the promoters under a lease with 15% escalation every three years (p. 129). No proceeds go to a subsidiary.

focus.title: Customer / supplier / geographic concentration
focus.detail: Top customer 25.21% / 21.86% / 19.36% of revenue FY26 / FY25 / FY24 (restated); top-5 40.84%, top-10 50.04%. In FY25 and FY24 the top 'customer' was the promoter's own proprietorship SMW II. On proforma basis top customer 11.59% (FY25). Top-10 suppliers 40.53% FY26 (76.68% FY25, 96.69% FY24); top supplier 7.94% FY26. No long-term agreements with suppliers or customers; distributors 46.16% and dealers 39.92% of FY26 revenue; dealer agreements terminable on 60 days' notice (p. 29). Exports 1.36% of FY26 revenue. Neither the 80% single-name test nor the top-10 test is met.

focus.title: Auditor qualifications / changes
focus.detail: No audit qualification on the financial statements. Rule 11(g) audit-trail remark: the accounting software did not record an audit trail at database level in FY24, FY25 and FY26 (to 31-Dec-2025; enabled January 2026). Risk factor discloses past disqualification of certain promoters / executive directors under Section 164 for directorship of Jaggatjit Agro Private Limited, which had not filed its financial statements / annual returns (p. 23). Statutory auditor: Anup Kumar Jain & Co. (FRN 005731N).

focus.title: CARO / audit trail
focus.detail: CARO 2020 Rule 11(g): audit trail feature not available at database level for FY24 and FY25 and, for FY26, until 31-Dec-2025. The issuer states no impact on the financial statements and that the feature was enabled in January 2026.

focus.title: Eligibility re-computation
focus.detail: Offer is made under Reg 6(2): the issuer does not meet Reg 6(1)(a) (net tangible assets of at least Rs 30 m in each of the three preceding years) or Reg 6(1)(c) (net worth of at least Rs 10 m in each of those years); FY24 net worth is Rs 5.32 m. Reg 32(2) then requires at least 75% of the Offer to be allotted to QIBs, otherwise the Offer fails. Not-more-than 15% to NIBs and 10% to retail.

focus.title: Lead-manager track record
focus.detail: DRHP gives Keynote's two IPOs in FY2026-27 (Amir Chand Jagdish Kumar (Exports) Ltd and CSM Technologies Ltd; both below issue price at 30 days) and none in FY2025-26 or FY2024-25. Both recorded in data/merchant_bankers.json. Current prices and issuer financials are not compiled.

focus.title: Valuation model guard
focus.detail: AMBER: DCF and relative diverge by -47.4% - the divergence is the finding; name its cause

focus.title: Valuation model guard
focus.detail: AMBER: TV above 75% of EV - DCF is mostly a terminal guess

focus.title: Data gap (high)
focus.detail: Price band, number of fresh shares, offer expenses and general corporate purposes amount

focus.title: Data gap (high)
focus.detail: Restated record is not like-for-like: FY26 is consolidated and includes the acquired SMW I and II businesses from 01-Apr-2025; FY24 and FY25 are the small standalone pre-acquisition Company. Only proforma FY25 / FY24 allow a like-for-like read, and the proforma has no cash flow statement or stub

focus.title: Data gap (high)
focus.detail: Interim (H1 FY27) financials; audited record ends 31-Mar-2026. Seasonality: Q4 revenue is lower (p. 24); the Kharif-season quarters are not disclosed

focus.title: Data gap (medium)
focus.detail: Reconciliation of proforma goodwill (Rs 65.66 m, FY25) to restated goodwill (Rs 4.55 m, FY26) and of proforma equity to restated equity

focus.title: Data gap (medium)
focus.detail: Land under the Dehlon plant (16.20 acres of a 30-acre promoter parcel) is leased from the promoters; lease terms for the Cheema plant and renewal rights are not in the summary pages

focus.title: Data gap (medium)
focus.detail: Subsidy receivable from State governments: amount and ageing not disclosed in the summary pages; DRHP notes past delays in payment

focus.title: Data gap (medium)
focus.detail: Pre-IPO placement of up to Rs 600 m not yet priced; would reduce the fresh issue

focus.title: Data gap (medium)
focus.detail: Only three listed peers, all tractor / tiller makers; the DRHP states no direct listed peer exists. Peer net debt (cash) not disclosed, so gross borrowings are used

focus.title: Data gap (medium)
focus.detail: Current price and 3-year financials of Keynote's two recent issues (merchant banker table)

focus.title: Data gap (medium)
focus.detail: Industry report is commissioned and paid for by the issuer (CARE Analytics and Advisory); independent size and share data not obtained

comfort.title: Bonus issue / share-count consistency
comfort.detail: Bonus 22:1 (allotted 27-May-2026) and split of Rs 10 to Rs 5 (4-May-2026) are applied retrospectively: EPS 5.64 / 1.42 / 0.57 and NAV Rs 12.75 use 55,650,984 shares. Check: Rs 313.90 m / 55.65 m = Rs 5.64. The FY26 balance sheet share capital of Rs 12.10 m is the pre-bonus count (1,209,804 shares of Rs 10) and is a presentation point.

comfort.title: Current vs deferred tax
comfort.detail: Current tax Rs 130.30 m on PBT of Rs 444.12 m = 29.3% in FY26 (statutory 25.17%); deferred tax was a small credit of Rs 0.09 m. FY25 current tax 16.1% of PBT and FY24 10.0% of PBT, both on the small pre-acquisition standalone Company. Tax paid in cash FY26 was Rs 104.52 m = 23.5% of PBT.

comfort.title: Revaluation reserve
comfort.detail: No revaluation reserve line; the DRHP states no shares have been issued out of revaluation reserve (p. 105).

comfort.title: Goodwill vs tangible equity
comfort.detail: Goodwill Rs 4.55 m = 0.6% of tangible net worth (Rs 704.74 m); it arises on the slump-sale acquisitions (consideration Rs 324.57 m against net assets Rs 320.03 m; Rs 3.05 m and Rs 1.50 m, Note 33). Proforma FY25 shows goodwill of Rs 65.66 m (p. 91) against Rs 4.55 m restated, a difference the DRHP does not reconcile in the summary.

comfort.title: Contingent liabilities
comfort.detail: Contingent liabilities Rs 71.70 m = 10.2% of tangible net worth (Rs 704.74 m): GST demands 22.67, income tax 0.18, other 6.50, bank guarantees 42.35. Rs 2.14 m of the GST demand relates to SMW I and is to be discharged by the Company under the business transfer terms.

comfort.title: Monitoring agency
comfort.detail: Offer exceeds Rs 1,000 m; the issuer will appoint a SEBI-registered credit rating agency as monitoring agency before filing the RHP.

comfort.title: Firm means of finance
comfort.detail: Objects are funded wholly from the Fresh Issue; no separate means-of-finance tie-up is required. Net proceeds are not appraised by any bank or financial institution (p. 125).

strengths: FY26 EBITDA Rs 557.38 m, margin 13.46%; proforma FY25 margin 14.51% (p. 157)
ROCE 31.10% and interest cover 5.03x in FY26 (p. 157)
Current tax Rs 130.30 m = 29.3% of PBT, above the statutory rate (p. 87)
Two integrated plants; FY26 utilisation 73.62% at Cheema and 89.68% at Dehlon (p. 267)
Issuer reports about 13% value share in straw reapers and 30% / 15% / 12% of subsidised super-seeder units in MP / Haryana / Punjab, from an issuer-commissioned report (p. 236)
weaknesses: FY26 CFO Rs 26.85 m against PAT Rs 313.90 m (p. 88)
Top customer 25.21% of FY26 revenue; no long-term agreements; dealer contracts terminable on 60 days' notice (pp. 29, 36)
Borrowings Rs 1,344.07 m; debt/equity 1.89x; 78.06% repayable within 12 months (pp. 157, 480)
Audit trail not enabled at database level to 31-Dec-2025 (p. 52)
Promoters disqualified in the past as directors of Jaggatjit Agro Pvt Ltd for non-filing (p. 24)
opportunities: Indian farm equipment market projected at 7.7% CAGR FY26-FY30 per the issuer-commissioned CARE report (p. 129)
Organised segment about 60% of the implements market, Rs 264 bn in FY26 to Rs 415 bn in FY30, per the same report (p. 221)
Rs 185 m of the proceeds repays borrowings (p. 124)
threats: Subsidy-linked demand; State payments have been delayed (p. 57)
Promoter-leased land under the Dehlon plant with 15% escalation every three years (p. 129)
Peers are far larger tractor makers; the DRHP names no direct listed peer (p. 156)
